st: Boil the extra potato in salted water for 20 minutes until soft, then drain and mash it until smooth. Let cool.
Mix the ground pork with half the onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Shape into 6 oval balls and set aside.
Grate the raw potatoes finely into a bowl, then squeeze them very hard in a clean towel over another bowl to remove the liquid.
Let the squeezed liquid sit for 5 minutes, pour off the water and keep the white starch at the bottom. Add the starch to the grated potato.
Add the mashed potato and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and mix into a sticky dough.
With wet hands, flatten a portion of dough, wrap it around a meatball and seal into a smooth oval. Repeat for all 6.
Bring a large pot of water with a good pinch of salt to a gentle simmer. Lower in the dumplings and cook for 30 minutes without letting them boil hard.
Meanwhile fry the bacon with the rest of the onion for 8 minutes until crisp and golden.
Check that the meat inside has reached 160°F (71°C). Drain and serve topped with the bacon and onion and a spoon of sour cream.
Wrap the beets in foil, roast at 400°F (200°C) for 1 hour, or boil them for 45 minutes, until tender. Cool, peel and grate.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 minutes until tender, then drain.
In a big bowl mix the grated beets and [[4 cups]] cold kefir. The soup will turn bright pink.
Stir in [[1 cup]] cold water, the cucumber, [[0.25 cup]] dill, scallions and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Chill the soup in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Taste and adjust salt. Ladle into bowls and add halved eggs and a spoon of sour cream.
Serve the hot potatoes on the side so each person can add them to the cold soup.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Fry the bacon in a skillet for 8 minutes until it begins to crisp. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes more. Do not drain.
Finely grate the potatoes into a large bowl. Pour off any liquid that collects.
Beat the eggs with [[1 cup]] warm milk, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Mix the eggs and the bacon mixture into the grated potatoes quickly, so the potatoes do not turn gray.
Pour into the dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until deep golden brown and a knife in the center comes out clean.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut into squares and serve with sour cream.

ing: cold, cubed, plus 1 tbsp soft for filling
st: Rub [[0.75 cup]] cold butter into [[3 cups]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Beat in 1 egg and add about [[0.5 cup]] cold water, a little at a time, until the dough just holds together. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Mix the lamb, onion, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and [[1 tbsp]] soft butter with your hands.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll the dough out to a quarter inch thick and cut circles about 4 inches wide.
Put a spoonful of filling on half of each circle, fold over, and crimp the edges with a fork.
Beat the second egg and brush it over the pastries. Cut a small slit in the top of each.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C). Serve warm.
Soak the casings in warm water for 30 minutes, then rinse them inside and out with running water.
Fry the bacon in a skillet for 6 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes more, then let cool.
Grate the potatoes finely, squeeze out as much liquid as you can, and put them in a bowl.
Add the ground pork, the bacon and onion with their fat, [[2 tsp]] salt, [[0.75 tsp]] pepper and [[0.25 cup]] milk. Mix well.
Tie one end of a casing and fill it loosely using a sausage stuffer or a wide funnel, leaving room because the potatoes swell. Tie the other end.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Prick the sausages with a pin and coil them in a greased baking dish.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, turning once, until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 10 minutes, slice and serve with sour cream or lingonberries.
Mix [[2 cups]] flour, the egg and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add about [[0.5 cup]] warm water slowly and knead for 5 minutes into a smooth, firm dough.
Cover the dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the pork, grated onion, [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper and [[2 tbsp]] cold water.
Roll the dough very thin on a floured counter and cut circles about 2.5 inches wide.
Place a small teaspoon of filling in each circle, fold in half and pinch the edges closed tightly.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Add the dumplings in batches.
Cook for 7 minutes after they float. Check one reaches 160°F (71°C) inside.
Drain and toss with the melted butter. Serve with sour cream.
Cut each slice of rye bread into sticks about half an inch wide.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the bread sticks in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt right away.
While the sticks are still hot, rub each one with the cut side of a garlic clove.
Pile the sticks on a plate and cover with the grated cheese. The heat will melt it slightly.
Serve warm with a dip, or with beer.

ing: softened, plus extra for the pan
st: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Grease the bottom and sides of a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat [[1 cup]] butter with [[0.5 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then [[1 tsp]] vanilla and the rum.
Beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt until foamy, then add the remaining [[0.5 cup]] sugar a spoonful at a time until stiff and glossy.
Fold [[1.5 cups]] flour into the yolk mix, then gently fold in the whites in two parts.
Spoon about a third of a cup of batter into the pan and tilt to spread it in a thin layer.
Bake for 5 minutes until golden. Pour on another thin layer and bake again. Repeat until the batter is used up, about 8 layers.
On the final layer, drag a fork upward through the soft batter every inch to pull up spikes, and bake until the spikes are dark golden.
Cool the cake in the pan for 20 minutes, then release and cool completely before slicing.
Mix [[2 cups]] flour, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and [[3 tbsp]] sour cream and stir into a stiff dough.
Knead for 5 minutes, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Cut the dough into small pieces and roll each into a thin rope, about the width of a pencil. Cut into pieces the size of a grain of rice.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the dough bits in small batches for 2 minutes until golden, and lift out with a slotted spoon.
Drain well on paper towels.
Warm [[1 cup]] honey in a large pot over low heat until runny. Do not boil.
Stir in the fried dough pieces until coated, then pile into a mound on a plate.
Sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] poppy seeds and let it set for 20 minutes before serving.
